newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on institutional sales.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on institutional sales.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Friday on speculative institutional selling, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 3,354 yuan ($404) per tonne, losing 38 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,433 yuan per tonne and hit a low of 3,348 yuan.
July fell 30 to 3,370, September 35 to 3,380 and November 25 to 3,395 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 28,800 tonnes from 12,300 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly lower and fell steadily for most of the session on institutional selling, traders said.
"Institutional selling was responsible for day's falls," one trader said.
"Rises in trading volume and open interest indicated big potential for further falls," he added. "But it also suggested investors' opinions were greatly mixed."
Traders said the presence of institutional investors would see a more active market in the short term.
